pages.text: The likeliest end: maximum entropy. After the black holes, an empty de Sitter space is left, with a horizon c/H away that glows at ħH/(2πk_B) ≈ 3×10⁻³⁰ K and holds S = πc⁵k_B/(GħH²) ≈ 2×10¹²² - the most entropy there can ever be. Nothing more can happen, because nothing can get colder than its surroundings.

Build the $(item)Entropy Horizon$(). It runs matter forward to the end: proton decay residue and a black hole's last flash become $(item)Heat Death Embers$() and $(fluid)Dark Era Haze$() - photons, neutrinos and positronium atoms wider than today's observable universe. Embers under dark energy give $(item)De Sitter Horizon Shards$(), and embers with a shard give $(item)Heat Death Remnants$().

In its Operation console the simulated age must pass 10³⁴ years (or the protons have not decayed); a faster expansion makes a smaller, hotter horizon - too hot, and it boils the containment. Horizon shards and phantom cells also make a $(item)Cosmological Constant$() in the Siphon.
